"''My blockade will intercept them.''"
"''They've destroyed the blockade. Our ships are just gone.|An [[Unidentified Imperial officer (Seventh Fleet)|Imperial officer]] informs Grand Admiral Thrawn about the destruction of his blockade, including many Dreadnoughts|audio=Purrgil_Blockade.flac|{{Rebels|Family Reunion – and Farewell}}}} The '''''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser''', also known as the '''Imperial Support Vessel''', the '''Dreadnought Support Vessel''', or the '''Rendili Dreadnought'''—alternatively spelled as the '''''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser''' or the '''Rendili Dreadnaught'''—was a powerful, midsize [[capital ship]] manufactured by [[Rendili StarDrive]]. The [[warship]] was designed for heavy [[Space warfare|space combat]] and [[planet]]ary occupation and was armed with a considerable number of [[turbolaser]]s and [[heavy laser cannon]]s. Featuring a thoroughly [[armor]]ed [[hull]] with minimal [[Deflector shield|shielding]], the [[heavy cruiser]] could carry an entire [[starfighter]] [[squadron]] in a dedicated [[hangar]]. Once utilized by the [[Utapaun Security Forces]] as anti-[[pirate]] vessels, as well as the [[Republic Navy]] to fight the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems|Separatists]] during the [[Clone Wars]], the Dreadnought was still considered one of the more capable [[Starship|ships]] of its class and size in use by the [[Imperial Era|time]] of the [[Galactic Empire]]. In the [[Standard year|year]] [[2 BBY]], a group of [[Batonn insurgents|insurgents]] from the planet [[Batonn]] employed a contingent of ''Dreadnought''-class vessels during a failed [[Batonn insurgency|revolt]], while many heavy [[cruiser]]s later served as part of [[Grand Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn's]] Imperial [[blockade]] over the planet [[Lothal]] in [[1 BBY]]. The blockade lasted until [[Liberation of Lothal|Lothal's liberation]] from the Empire, when all Imperial ships present were destroyed by a pod of the [[Realspace|space]]-faring [[purrgil]] creatures. The ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser was also used by the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]] in the faction's [[Galactic Civil War|struggle]] against the Empire. Many former Imperial Support Vessels, which the Empire did not see worth the price of repair and simply left to deteriorate, were salvaged and outfitted to serve in the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|Alliance Fleet]]. In [[4 ABY]], the rebels used a [[Thief|stolen]] Imperial Support Vessel, [[49AX3]], to [[Troop transport|transport]] their [[Rebel trooper|soldiers]] for a [[Raid at Imperial Refining Platform M36|raid]] at an [[Imperial Refining Platform M36|Imperial refinery]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories|Outer Rim]], securing the [[Refinery|installation's]] [[fuel]] supplies for the rebel [[fleet]]. ==Characteristics== {{Quote|Load up the ''shuttles''! We've gotta ''evac''!|Commander Luke Skywalker, to a rebel trooper|}} [[File:49AX3-AORLuke1.jpg|thumb|left|235px|The Imperial Support Vessel was equipped with twelve sublight engines.]] The ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser, otherwise known as the Imperial Support Vessel, the Dreadnought Support Vessel,{{SWKidsYouTube|series=Star Wars By the Numbers|text=Every Type of Ship in Rebels|video=iasSt3JSV4Q|date=2019-10-31|nolive=1}} or the Rendili Dreadnought, was an oblong, midsize [[capital ship]] class manufactured by [[Rendili StarDrive]]. Alternatively spelled as the ''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser or the Rendili Dreadnaught, the [[heavy cruiser]] had a [[Color|gray]], heavily [[armor]]ed [[hull]] along with several elliptical or rectangular protrusions amidship. The [[starship]] could sustain a considerable amount of damage despite being equipped with minimal [[deflector shield]]s, not to mention the hull redundancies that prevented [[atmosphere]] from venting into [[Realspace|space]] during combat.''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]'' While the exterior of the customizable craft had a [[clam]]shell-like or rectangular bow, the interior featured a [[Bridge (starship)|bridge]] and [[viewport]]s at the bow{{SW|url=series/star-wars-rebels/a-fools-hope-trivia-gallery|text="A Fool's Hope" Trivia Gallery}} {{C|Slide 3}} and sides. [[File:Dreadnought-SaS.png|thumb|right|220px|The ''Dreadnought''-class was a powerful and versatile warship.]] The ''Dreadnought''-class included multiple [[Hangar|launch bays]] and could carry [[shuttle]]s along with a single [[squadron]] of twelve [[starfighter]]s in a dedicated hangar. It possessed twelve [[sublight engine]]s in varying shapes and sizes, which rendered the vessel one of the fastest ships of its class at sublight speeds. The craft also held a primary [[hyperdrive]] rating of Class 4, with a backup at Class 18, as well as a Class 2. Depending on the configuration, the Dreadnought [[cruiser]] could hold 9,000 to 16,000 [[officer]]s, [[pilot]]s, and enlisted crew, as well as 3,000 [[troop]]s. The craft contained enough consumables to last one [[Standard year|year]] for the crew and marketed at 7,200,000 [[Galactic Credit Standard|credits]]. Designed to support multiple [[weapon]] configurations, the versatile and powerful Dreadnought carried an impressive number of [[turbolaser]]s—it possessed five forward and five aft twin medium turbolaser batteries, along with ten port and ten starboard quad light turbolasers. The [[warship]] was also equipped with five port and five starboard [[heavy laser cannon]]s for anti-starfighter defense, a [[Navigation computer|navicomputer]], and medium-range [[sensor]]s, including a dorsal [[Rectenna|sensor dish]] located near the stern of the vessel. Additionally, the ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruisers used by the [[Batonn insurgents]] boasted red hull markings, a trait shared by other insurgent starships. ==Role== [[File:49AX3Combat-AORLuke1.jpg|thumb|left|255px|The ''Dreadnought''-class cruiser was made for heavy space combat.]] Designed for heavy [[Space warfare|space combat]] and [[planet]]ary occupation, the ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruisers were commonly used to haul cargo and carry out various missions that larger crafts were unable to undertake. Dreadnought [[Commanding officer|commanders]] endeavored to move the ponderous vehicle into position to fire broadsides at hostiles to gain superiority in combat. Firing the ship's turbolasers and heavy [[laser cannon]]s in minion groups of at least three would also increase the chance of hitting smaller and faster enemy starfighters and [[gunboat]]s. To counter the attack of rival [[bomber]]s, the cruiser deployed and gave firing cover for its fighters. The ''Dreadnought''-class was used as a workhorse cruiser by the [[Navy|navies]] of both the [[Galactic Empire]] and its opponent, the [[Alliance to Restore the Republic|Rebel Alliance]], for miscellaneous purposes. While the [[Imperial Navy]] made use of the vessels to protect its worlds and [[Space station|stations]], the Dreadnought served as a mobile base of operations for the latter faction's [[battle group]]s. ==History== ===Era of the Republic=== [[File:Carrack_Cruiser_FFno106.png|thumb|right|250px|The ''Carrack''-class light cruisers (pictured) served as escorts for the Dreadnoughts in the Republic Navy.]] Once quite common in [[the galaxy]], the ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser was considered old and antiquated at the [[First Battle of Geonosis|outbreak]] of the pan-[[Galaxy|galactic]] [[Clone Wars]] between the [[Galactic Republic]] and the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems]] in the year [[22 BBY]].''[[Star Wars: Timelines]]'' The [[Republic Navy]] deployed ''Dreadnought''-class ships escorted by smaller [[Carrack-class light cruiser|''Carrack''-class light cruisers]] during the war. One Republic Dreadnought was the ''[[Mas Ramdar]]'', which, along with three ''Carrack''-class cruisers, formed [[Home Fleet Strike Group Five]] as part of the [[Coruscant Home Defense Fleet|Coruscant Home Fleet]] tasked with protecting the Republic's [[capital]] planet of [[Coruscant]]. Led by [[Lieutenant Commander]] [[Lorth Needa]], Strike Group Five participated in the [[Battle of Coruscant]] of [[19 BBY]]. During the battle, the group trapped the Separatist [[General]] [[Grievous]]' [[flagship]] ''[[Invisible Hand]]'', aboard which [[Supreme Chancellor]] [[Darth Sidious|Sheev Palpatine]], leader of the Republic, was held [[Prisoner|captive]]. However, Needa, who did not believe that Palpatine was aboard the [[Providence-class Dreadnought|ship]], demanded the general's surrender and gave him ten [[Standard minute|minutes]] to prove his claims before the strike group's cruisers opened fire. Grievous did not surrender, but [[Jedi General]]s [[Obi-Wan Kenobi]] and [[Anakin Skywalker]] rescued the [[Chancellor]]. Around that [[time]], the [[Planetary defense forces|defense forces]] of the planet [[Utapau]], known as the [[Utapaun Security Forces]],{{HelmetCollectionCite|25|Weapons & Uniforms}} utilized downscaled ships such as the Rendili Dreadnoughts, which were used as anti-[[pirate]] vessels. Their largest Dreadnought was one-fifth the size of a [[Lucrehulk-class battleship|''Lucrehulk''-class battleship]], a circular craft that was 3,170 [[meter]]s, or 10,400 [[Foot|feet]], in diameter. Sometime later, after the war [[Mission to Mustafar|ended]] and the Republic [[Proclamation of the New Order|transformed]] into the Empire in 19 [['ABY-BBY' dating system|BBY]], a [[Unidentified Dreadnought-class heavy cruiser|Dreadnought]] that bore Republic markings suffered damage and emerged from [[hyperspace]] near an abandoned Republic supply depot. Broadcasting a [[Distress signal|distress call]] to any [[Republic Military|Republic forces]], the vessel had young [[clone trooper]]s on board who knew nothing of the Galactic Empire's existence. ===Batonn insurgency=== {{Quote|Incoming! Ten ships on vector one-ten by 80. Batonn insurgents!''"
"''Two more groups incoming. Eleven vessels each. Admiral, they're targeting the cruisers.|Imperial [[sensor officer]]s, reporting to Admiral Thrawn|}} [[File:BatonnSupportVessel-Thrawn6.jpg|thumb|left|275px|One of the Batonn insurgents' Dreadnought cruisers under fire from the ''Chimaera'']] At some point in the [[Imperial Era]], a Dreadnought cruiser flew near an Imperial hangar bay that housed a [[YT-2000 light freighter]].{{Destiny|set=Star Wars: Destiny Two-Player Game|cardname=Hangar Bay—Imperial Fleet|link=https://swdestinydb.com/card/04023}} In [[2 BBY]], a group of insurgents led by the [[smuggler]] [[Nevil Cygni]] on the planet [[Batonn]] used a contingent of Dreadnought Support Vessels in [[Batonn insurgency|battle]] against the Empire. Several of the vessels were part of the insurgent attack squadrons that opposed [[Admiral]] [[Mitth'raw'nuruodo|Thrawn's]] [[96th Task Force|naval forces]] [[orbit]]ing Batonn at the [[Siege of the Creekpath Mining and Refining complex|siege]] of the [[Creekpath Mining and Refining complex]]. Although the insurgents targeted Thrawn's [[Arquitens-class light cruiser|''Arquitens''-class light cruisers]], they were defeated by the [[Imperial Military|Imperial forces]]. The vast majority[[Thrawn (novel)|''Thrawn'']] of the rebel forces were destroyed by Imperial [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter|TIE fighters]] and Thrawn's flagship, the [[Imperial I-class Star Destroyer|Imperial Star Destroyer]] ''[[Chimaera]]'', due to Thrawn anticipating Cygni's strategy. ===Galactic Civil War=== ====In service of both sides==== The ''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser was in service of both the Galactic Empire and the Rebel Alliance during the [[Galactic Civil War]]. Although the vessel was still regarded as one of the more capable ships of its class and size in use at that time, the Dreadnought had become increasingly rare during the conflict; the stress of combat, accidents, or simply fatigue would cause the ship to deteriorate, while the scarcity of the model's parts only increased. [[File:Paragon_SWArmada.png|thumb|right|290px|The Assault Frigate Mark II series (pictured) was derived from the old ''Dreadnought''-class.]] Considering that the craft also required a large crew and was equipped with outdated systems, the Empire did not see the Dreadnoughts as worth the price of repair, and broken vessels were left abandoned in [[shipyard]]s or in orbit above planets. On the other hand, many former Imperial Support Vessels were salvaged, refitted, and absorbed into the [[Rebel Alliance Navy|rebel fleet]] as [[Alliance officer|rebel commanders]] relied heavily on [[Starfighter combat|fighter tactics]], and the ''Dreadnought''-class could carry an entire squadron of starfighters in a given hangar—an extremely attractive feature for the Alliance. The large number of modifications made to the ''Dreadnought''-class by the early Rebel Alliance also spawned another series of capital ships known as the [[Assault Frigate Mark II]]. Bearing little resemblance to the original Dreadnought, much of the starship's structure was either altered or completely removed, which resulted in a considerable reduction in the number of personnel required to operate the warship and a decrease in the vehicle's endurance for damage in favor of improving the vessel's maneuverability and speed while maintaining its armament. ====Mystery of the ''Enigma'' and Imperial blockade of Lothal==== {{Quote|Um… Was that the plan? Because we're all clear up here. There are no Imperial ships left.|Commander [[Wolffe]], after witnessing the purrgil destroying Imperial starships|audio=WolffeLothal.flac|}} [[File:Thrawn_blockade.png|thumb|left|255px|An Imperial Support Vessel (bottom) in the Imperial blockade over Lothal]] First commissioned in the [[Republic Era|time]] of the Old Republic, the [[Enigma (Dreadnought-class)|''Enigma'']] was an old ''Dreadnought''-class cruiser deployed by the Alliance Fleet. Allegedly a haunted vessel, the ship suffered power fluctuations, while the vessel's new parts inexplicably broke or disappeared, and even some of its crew vanished aboard the craft. Although these events could have been caused by an Imperial [[saboteur]], some crew believed that the ship was actually cursed, claiming that they had seen [[Ghost (folklore)|ghosts]] wandering the Dreadnought's corridors. The Imperial Support Vessel was one of the starship classes that served as part of [[Grand Admiral]] Thrawn's [[Seventh Fleet (Galactic Empire)|Seventh Fleet]] during its [[blockade]] over the planet [[Lothal]] amid ongoing [[Lothal campaign|conflict]] with local [[Lothal resistance group|rebel forces]]. The blockade ultimately proved unable to contain the rebel presence on Lothal. After the rebel [[VCX-100 light freighter|light freighter]] ''[[Ghost]]'' sneaked through the blockade by attaching itself to a passing [[Cargo freighter EF-75|cargo freighter]]{{Rebels|A Fool's Hope}} in [[1 BBY]], the Lothal resistance, led by [[Jedi]] [[Padawan]] [[Ezra Bridger]], launched a final attack on the [[Lothal garrison|Imperial forces]] and [[Liberation of Lothal|liberated Lothal]] from its occupation. During the engagement, the entire blockade, including many Imperial Support Vessels, was destroyed by a pod of [[purrgil]]—massive, [[whale]]-like creatures capable of naturally traveling through hyperspace—as part of Bridger's plan. ====Raid at Imperial Refining Platform M36==== {{Quote|We just secured a ''year's worth'' of fuel for the fleet. If we jump through an ''asteroid'', we wouldn't just blow ''ourselves''—we'd blow up the ''Rebellion's hopes''.|A Pau'an rebel major|}} [[File:ISVBridge-AORLuke1.jpg|thumb|right|255px|A Pau'an rebel major aboard Imperial Support Vessel 49AX3's bridge]] In [[4 ABY]], a team of [[Rebel trooper|Rebel Alliance soldiers]] led by a [[Pau'an]] [[Unidentified Rebel major (Pau'an)|major]] undertook a [[Raid at Imperial Refining Platform M36|raid]] at [[Imperial Refining Platform M36]] in the [[Outer Rim Territories]], using the [[Thief|stolen]] Imperial Support Vessel [[49AX3]] as a [[troop transport]]. Assisted by the Jedi [[Commander]] [[Luke Skywalker]] and his [[T-65B X-wing starfighter]], the rebels seized the [[refinery]]'s [[fuel]] supplies for their [[fleet]], but their escape was blocked by an [[Imperial II-class Star Destroyer|''Imperial II''-class Star Destroyer]] after the Pau'an refused to enter hyperspace through the surrounding [[asteroid field]]. Meanwhile, far from the refinery, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith|Sith Lord]] and [[Galactic Emperor]] Palpatine showed Skywalker a [[Force vision|vision]] through [[the Force]] in which the rebels' Dreadnought would be destroyed, in hopes of breaking the Jedi's will to aid the Rebellion. Skywalker, however, escaped the [[Emperor]]'s vision and landed his [[X-wing starfighter|X-wing]] in the Imperial Support Vessel's hangar after destroying several attacking Imperial [[TIE series|TIE]] fighters. He and the [[major]] then used the latter's private shuttle to draw away the attention of the remaining TIEs. The tactic succeeded, and the rebels aboard 49AX3 were able to escape, fleeing to a nearby world. ==Behind the scenes== ===Reintroduction into ''Star Wars'' canon=== [[File:Rebels_Dreadnaught.jpg|thumb|left|270px|Concept art of the Imperial Support Vessel by Andre Kirk]] The ''Dreadnaught''-class heavy cruiser was first mentioned in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in the [[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon 52|fifty-second issue]] of the ''[[Star Wars: Build the Millennium Falcon]]'' magazine, published by [[De Agostini]] around [[December 30]], [[2015]].{{BMFdates|52}} The ship model later received its first depiction via the [[Star Wars: Destiny Two-Player Game|''Two-Player Game'']] expansion for the [[Star Wars: Destiny|''Star Wars'': Destiny]] collectible dice and card game, which uses repurposed artwork from the [[2014]] [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] [[Star Wars Roleplaying|roleplaying game]] book [[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]][[Star Wars: Age of Rebellion Core Rulebook|''Star Wars: Age of Rebellion'' Core Rulebook]] by artist [[Adam Lane]]. The ''Star Wars'': Destiny card depicting the ship, titled "Hangar Bay—Imperial Fleet," was revealed on [[Fantasy Flight Games]]' [https://www.fantasyflightgames.com official website] on [[August 31]], [[2017]], a day before the product's release.{{FantasyFlightGames|url=en/news/2017/8/31/star-wars-destiny-two-player-game|text=Star Wars: Destiny Two-Player Game|date=2017-08-31}} The ''Dreadnought''-class made its first appearance as a background ship in "[[A Fool's Hope]]," the penultimate episode in the [[Star Wars Rebels Season Four|final season]] of the ''[[Star Wars Rebels]]'' animated series, which first aired on [[March 5]], [[2018]].{{SW|url=news/the-final-episodes-of-star-wars-rebels-begin-february-19-on-disney-xd|text=The Final Episodes of ''Star Wars Rebels'' Begin February 19 on Disney XD|date=2018-01-19}} The cruiser's colloquial name, Imperial Support Vessel, was revealed through a concept art illustration by [[Andre Kirk]] in the accompanying "A Fool's Hope" episode guide on [[StarWars.com]]. The designs for the Imperial Support Vessel seen in the episode were derived from the [[Dreadnaught-class heavy cruiser/Legends|Imperial Dreadnaught]], which figured prominently in [[Star Wars: The Thrawn Trilogy|''The Thrawn Trilogy'']], a Legends novel series written by [[Timothy Zahn]].''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]'' While the Dreadnaught first appeared in the trilogy's second entry, [[1992]]'s ''[[Dark Force Rising]]'',''[[Dark Force Rising]]'' the ship originated in the [[1989]] ''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'', written by [[Greg Gorden]] and published by [[West End Games]] for ''[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game]]''.''[[Imperial Sourcebook]]'' Both the craft's new ''Star Wars Rebels'' design and old Legends appearance continued to be used to depict the vehicle in canon media. ===Alternate naming and inconsistencies=== [[File:Dreadnaught_2048x1380.png|thumb|right|275px|The ''Dreadnaught''-class debuted in West End Games' ''Imperial Sourcebook''.]] The 2018 reference book [[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'']] first identified the vessel as the Rendili Dreadnaught.[[Star Wars: Complete Vehicles (2018)|''Star Wars: Complete Vehicles'' (2018)]] While the book's [[2020]] edition, ''[[Star Wars Complete Vehicles, New Edition]]'', uses the same name and spelling in the text, the index entry for the ship was changed to "Rendili Dreadnought." The [[2019]] reference book ''[[Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition]]'' also introduced the vehicle's model as "''Dreadnought''-class" with the new spelling. Unlike other sources, the book does not capitalize the colloquial name, rendering it as "Imperial support vessel." Additionally, "Every Type of Ship in ''Star Wars Rebels''," an [[October 31]], 2019 installment of the ''[[Star Wars By the Numbers]]'' web series created for [[StarWarsKids.com]], identified the ship as "Dreadnought Support Vessel." Fantasy Flight Games' 2020 [[roleplaying game]] sourcebook ''[[Starships and Speeders]]'' provided the vehicle's full technical name as "''Dreadnought''-class heavy cruiser," with the same spelling for the word "Dreadnought." Although ''Ultimate Star Wars, New Edition'' initially established that the ''Dreadnought''-class was equipped with a Class 2 hyperdrive, ''Starships and Speeders'' later stated that the ship held a primary hyperdrive rating of Class 4 along with a backup hyperdrive rating of Class 18. This article assumes the latter and more recent source is correct. The 2020 book ''[[The Art of Star Wars Rebels]]'' also erroneously identifies the vessel as a [[light cruiser]]. ==Appearances== {{Mediacat|imagecat=Images of Dreadnought-class heavy cruisers}}
